content.thinking: The Israeli savings-fund page lists 182 tracks from 15 companies, with fees from 0.15% to 2%, but the regulator's data here hasn't been updated since September 2026. I'm moving on to the government-bond track next.

The table is hard to parse: government bond funds show low returns over 3 and 5 years, the share fund shows 22.07%, and I can't tell what the "מט"ח" circles mean or which company this is. I'll keep reading to find the company name.

Claude writes: The table's grey row "מור" with 14 tracks is a company I don't recognize, and the monetary row "כספי (שקלי)" shows 4.43% over 3 years and 3.45% over 5. I'll scroll through the two remaining screens next, since the text is hard to read on this background.
I'm going through the Phoenix, Altshuler Shaham and other fund options, and the numbers are blurring together, so I'll stop here.

input.answer: I didn't decide anything. If I had to say, the safe-sounding ones were "גמל אג"ח ממשלות" (0.52% fee, 4.9% over 3 years) and the "כספי (שקלי)" tracks at הפניקס (0.57%, 4.4%), but I'll ask you or the bank before I move anything.

stuck.why: The table starts in the middle with no company name, so I didn't know whose tracks the first rows were. I only saw company names later in grey rows (מור, הפניקס, אלטשולר שחם).
"נתוני הרשות לא עודכנו מאז ספטמבר 2026": I wasn't sure if I could trust the numbers at all.
Little circles in two colours and percentages above 100% (101%, 103%). I couldn't understand it.
"פחות מ־3 שנים" where I expected a number, and I wasn't sure if 4.9% over 3 years is per year or for the whole time.
